name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Pfluger running with large financial advantage ($2.9M cash vs $47K)
Challenger Reynolds underfunded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: Pfluger holds a deep-red West Texas seat, is renominated, and outpaces Reynolds in cash by a wide margin, while markets price a Republican win near certainty. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a sudden national wave toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though neither appears likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This West Texas seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the state, with a partisan lean of about seventeen points toward the GOP. August Pfluger, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: roughly $2.9 million in cash on hand against about $47,000 for Democratic challenger Claire Reynolds, who has raised under $90,000 and drawn no outside spending.

Prediction markets give the Republican side roughly a ninety-four percent chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided resource gap, all of which point to a safe Republican hold.
